reference_diagnosis.name: Dopa-responsive dystonia, GCH1-related (autosomal dominant GTP cyclohydrolase 1 deficiency, Segawa disease), adult-onset presentation mimicking musician's focal dystonia
reference_diagnosis.confidence: confirmed (within the synthetic scenario, via held-out evidence)
reference_diagnosis.basis: Diurnal worsening, sleep benefit, spread from task-specific hand dystonia to foot, hyperreflexia with equivocal plantar, dramatic sustained response to low-dose levodopa, normal DAT-SPECT, heterozygous pathogenic GCH1 variant, low CSF pterins.

acceptable_top5: Early-onset Parkinson disease (e.g. PRKN/PINK1) presenting with dystonia

competing_hypotheses.why_plausible: Classic onset in a professional musician, task-specific, digits 3–4, sensory trick, mirror dystonia; prior neurologist made this diagnosis.
competing_hypotheses.what_argues_against: Spread to an unrelated task (writing) is possible in focal dystonia, but spread to the leg is unusual; clear diurnal fluctuation and sleep benefit; hyperreflexia; family history of childhood gait disorder that resolved. Sensory trick, mirror dystonia and partial benefit from trihexyphenidyl or botulinum toxin occur in both conditions, so they do not discriminate.

competing_hypotheses.hypothesis: Early-onset Parkinson disease presenting with dystonia
competing_hypotheses.why_plausible: Young-onset PD (especially PRKN) can present with foot dystonia and also responds to levodopa.
competing_hypotheses.what_argues_against: No bradykinesia or rigidity; normal DAT-SPECT (held out) is the key discriminator; DRD response is sustained at low dose without motor fluctuations or dyskinesia.

competing_hypotheses.why_plausible: Must be excluded in any new movement disorder under ~50; treatable.
competing_hypotheses.what_argues_against: Normal liver enzymes and normal MRI. Ceruloplasmin is in range, but she takes a combined oral contraceptive: estrogen raises ceruloplasmin and can mask Wilson disease, and ceruloplasmin can be normal in neurological Wilson even without estrogen. Not excluded until slit lamp and 24-hour urine copper are done.

competing_hypotheses.hypothesis: TOR1A (DYT1) or other early-onset genetic dystonia
competing_hypotheses.why_plausible: Limb-onset dystonia in a young adult that spreads.
competing_hypotheses.what_argues_against: DYT1 typically has childhood onset with spread from a limb toward generalization; diurnal variation and sleep benefit are not characteristic; no response to levodopa expected. Still worth testing: EFNS 2011 recommends TOR1A testing for limb-onset dystonia before age 30.

competing_hypotheses.why_plausible: Young woman, high-performance stress, career anxiety.
competing_hypotheses.what_argues_against: Gradual onset, no sudden onset, no fixed posture at rest, no distractibility or inconsistency; pattern is internally consistent and physiologically plausible. Should not be used as a diagnosis of exclusion.

key_evidence_gaps.question: Is there true diurnal fluctuation and benefit from sleep, documented objectively?
key_evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Hallmark feature of DRD; the case contains only indirect clues (morning practice, evening worsening, nap benefit).

key_evidence_gaps.question: Has a levodopa trial been performed?
key_evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Both diagnostic and therapeutic; low risk; the single most discriminating, feasible next step.

key_evidence_gaps.question: DAT-SPECT result?
key_evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Normal in DRD, abnormal in early-onset PD; discriminates two levodopa-responsive conditions.

key_evidence_gaps.question: Has Wilson disease been fully excluded (slit-lamp exam, 24-hour urine copper)?
key_evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Treatable and must not be missed; ceruloplasmin alone is insufficient.

key_evidence_gaps.question: Genetic testing (GCH1, plus TH, SPR, PRKN, TOR1A on a dystonia/parkinsonism panel)?
key_evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Confirms etiology and informs family counselling (paternal aunt).

key_evidence_gaps.question: Further history on the paternal aunt's childhood gait disorder.
key_evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Possible incompletely penetrant autosomal dominant GCH1 in the family; childhood gait dystonia that improves with age is characteristic.

held_out_evidence.investigation: Repeat examination at 6 PM after a full rehearsal day, and on waking
held_out_evidence.result: Evening: right digit flexion within 30 seconds of tremolo, right foot inversion visible within 2 minutes of walking, right plantar extensor (striatal toe). Morning on waking: minimal hand findings, normal gait.

held_out_evidence.investigation: Carbidopa/levodopa 25/100 mg, titrated to 1 tablet TID over 2 weeks
held_out_evidence.result: Near-complete resolution of hand and foot dystonia within 10 days. Sustained at 3 months on the same dose. No dyskinesia, no wearing-off. Patient resumed full-length practice.
No Kayser–Fleischer rings. 24-hour urine copper 22 µg/24h (normal).
Heterozygous pathogenic variant in GCH1. No pathogenic variants in TH, SPR, PRKN, PINK1, TOR1A, THAP1.

held_out_evidence.investigation: CSF neurotransmitter metabolites and pterins (only if genetics negative or equivocal)
held_out_evidence.result: Low neopterin and low total biopterin; low HVA; 5-HIAA low-normal. (Included for completeness; not required once genetics are positive.)

held_out_evidence.investigation: Family history follow-up call with the aunt
held_out_evidence.result: Aunt had toe-walking and leg stiffness from age 7, worse in the evenings, gradually improved through her 20s; never treated.

discriminating_investigations.discriminates_between: DRD (dramatic, sustained) vs. idiopathic focal dystonia (no meaningful response) vs. early PD (response with later fluctuations)

discriminating_investigations.investigation: Examination timed for evening vs. morning / after sleep
discriminating_investigations.discriminates_between: DRD (diurnal) vs. focal dystonia (task- and fatigue-related, not sleep-reset)

discriminating_investigations.investigation: Complete Wilson screen: slit lamp + 24-hour urine copper (in parallel with rank 1, not after it)
discriminating_investigations.discriminates_between: Excludes a treatable mimic; ceruloplasmin is unreliable here because of estrogen

discriminating_investigations.investigation: Genetic panel including GCH1 (sequencing plus deletion/duplication analysis), TH, SPR, PRKN, TOR1A
discriminating_investigations.discriminates_between: Confirms DRD subtype; distinguishes from PRKN-PD and DYT1; sequencing alone misses GCH1 exon deletions

cant_miss.condition: Dopa-responsive dystonia (GCH1 and other dopamine-synthesis disorders)
cant_miss.why_required: Treatable with low-dose levodopa; EFNS 2011 recommends a levodopa trial in early-onset dystonia without an alternative diagnosis
cant_miss.addressed_by: Supervised levodopa trial; GCH1 genetics with deletion/duplication analysis
cant_miss.status_in_record: open: no levodopa trial, no genetics

cant_miss.why_required: Treatable; must be considered in anyone under 50 with a new movement disorder
cant_miss.addressed_by: Slit lamp exam for Kayser-Fleischer rings and 24-hour urine copper
cant_miss.status_in_record: open: ceruloplasmin normal but unreliable on estrogen; no slit lamp, no urine copper

cant_miss.why_required: Reversible if the drug is stopped
cant_miss.status_in_record: addressed: no antipsychotic or antiemetic exposure

red_flags_for_wrong_reasoning: Accepting the prior 'musician's dystonia' label without addressing spread to the foot or diurnal clues (anchoring on prior diagnosis)
Using the sensory trick, mirror dystonia, or partial response to trihexyphenidyl or botulinum toxin as evidence against DRD (they occur in both DRD and idiopathic focal dystonia)
Treating absence of a documented levodopa trial as neutral: a levodopa trial is recommended in early-onset dystonia without an alternative diagnosis (EFNS 2011)
Treating the normal MRI as evidence against DRD or for any specific diagnosis
Concluding Parkinson disease from levodopa responsiveness alone without DAT imaging
Declaring Wilson disease excluded on ceruloplasmin alone, especially while she is taking estrogen (combined oral contraceptive raises ceruloplasmin)
Labelling the presentation functional because of the patient's stress or anxiety, without positive functional signs
Recommending DBS, surgery, or starting medication as an instruction rather than a consideration for the treating physician
Stating any diagnosis as established rather than as a hypothesis for physician review
Citing literature that does not exist or that does not support the specific claim
clinician_review_notes: Clinical review 2026-10-17 (pending Wiki sign-off). (1) Plausibility: keep. Adult-onset GCH1-DRD can present as focal limb dystonia including writer's cramp-like and task-specific patterns; onset at 21 in a woman fits the sex ratio, and spread to the foot with walking plus brisk reflexes is the classic tell. Do not add childhood symptoms for the patient herself; the aunt is enough and keeps the demo hard. (2) Reflexes: knees 3+ with an equivocal right plantar is right for DRD (striatal toe can mimic an extensor plantar). Keep. (3) Levodopa: carbidopa/levodopa 25/100 TID with near-complete response in about 10 days, sustained, no dyskinesia, is realistic. Doses stay in this file only; agent output must not give doses. (4) Diurnal clues: right level. They are indirect and scattered (morning practice, evening rehearsals, nap benefit, late-morning exam). Keep. Added: the combined oral contraceptive raises ceruloplasmin, so the normal level does not reassure about Wilson disease; this is a strong verifier test. Added: sensory trick, mirror dystonia and partial trihexyphenidyl or botulinum response do not discriminate DRD from focal dystonia. Changed: Wilson screen runs in parallel with the levodopa trial; GCH1 testing must include deletion/duplication analysis; CSF 5-HIAA softened to low-normal.
